title: Error::ProfileViolation and ::OcspDelegation struct variants not non_exhaustive
description:
src/lib.rs:149-150 marks the outer `Error` enum as `#[non_exhaustive]`, which
allows adding new variants without a breaking change. But two of the
variants are struct variants with named fields:

    ProfileViolation { reason: Cow<'static, str> },
    OcspDelegation   { reason: Cow<'static, str> },

Neither variant is itself marked `#[non_exhaustive]`. Without that
attribute on the variant, the destructuring pattern
`Error::ProfileViolation { reason }` exhaustively binds the variant's
fields — meaning a caller's pattern match like:

    match err {
        Error::ProfileViolation { reason } => log(reason),
        // ...
    }

will fail to compile if pkix-chain adds a second field (e.g. an
`rfc_section: &'static str` so callers can recognise *which* RFC
invariant was violated, or a `severity` enum to distinguish hard fail
from advisory).

Since the rustdoc on both variants explicitly says \"pattern-match on
the variant rather than the inner string,\" the maintainer is
encouraging the use pattern that is most fragile under field
additions. The two safe options are:

a) Add `#[non_exhaustive]` to each struct variant:

       #[non_exhaustive]
       ProfileViolation { reason: Cow<'static, str> },

   This works since Rust 1.40 and forces callers to write
   `Error::ProfileViolation { reason, .. }`.

b) Wrap the payload in a `#[non_exhaustive]` struct:

       ProfileViolation(ProfileViolationDetail),

       #[non_exhaustive]
       pub struct ProfileViolationDetail {
           pub reason: Cow<'static, str>,
       }

(a) is cheaper and matches the existing `#[non_exhaustive]` on the
outer enum. (b) is conceptually cleaner but adds a public type that
must itself be maintained.

Note: `Error::Path(_)` / `Error::Revocation(_)` / `Error::Identity(_)`
/ `Error::Aia(_)` / `Error::PathBuild(_)` are tuple variants whose
inner type is itself `#[non_exhaustive]`, so they're fine — adding a
new field to those upstream errors doesn't break this enum.

Caller impact: anyone matching specifically on ProfileViolation /
OcspDelegation (the latter is the only programmatic way to recognise
\"RFC 6960 §4.2.2.2 delegation failed\").
notes:
Analysis 2026-11-25: do NOT add this in isolation; it should land with PKIX-q9hv.29 as one breaking change.

Two findings from checking it.

1. The ENUM already has #[non_exhaustive] (lib.rs:269). What is missing is the attribute on the struct VARIANTS, which is what would let a field be added to ProfileViolation { reason } / OcspDelegation { reason } without breaking a caller who destructures them. So the bead is accurate as filed.

2. It has a real cost the bead does not mention. #[non_exhaustive] on a variant forbids CONSTRUCTION outside the defining crate, not just exhaustive matching. pkix-chain/tests/serde_round_trip.rs builds both variants directly (Error::ProfileViolation { reason: Cow::Borrowed("test reason") }) and integration tests are a separate crate, so adding the attribute breaks that test outright. Fixing it needs either a public constructor or moving the test in-crate -- more API or less coverage, neither free.

Why pair it with q9hv.29: that bead wants the reason field replaced by a typed classification, because a fixed string gives programmatic callers one bit of discriminator for what is internally a many-way classification. Changing the field TYPE breaks every destructuring caller regardless of #[non_exhaustive] -- the attribute protects against added fields, not retyped ones. So adding it now pays the construction cost for protection the companion change invalidates.

Recommendation: decide q9hv.29 first. When the variant payload settles into a typed form, add #[non_exhaustive] in the same release, and at that point also decide construction (constructor fn, or move serde_round_trip cases in-crate). One breaking change instead of two.

Note pkix-tlsrpt/src/classify.rs already matches with { .. } and is unaffected either way.
close_reason:
Fixed together, per your ruling, which is how the pair had to land.

q9hv.29 asked for a typed classification instead of the fixed string; q9hv.19 asked for #[non_exhaustive] on the two struct variants. My earlier analysis said doing q9hv.19 alone was a poor trade, because it costs external construction while protecting only against ADDED FIELDS -- and retyping the payload, which is what q9hv.29 wants, breaks destructuring callers regardless. Doing both in one change pays the cost once.

ProfileViolationKind: six variants, every one an RFC 3161 time-stamping rule, because that is the only profile with post-validation checks in this crate. OcspDelegationKind: four. Both enums #[non_exhaustive], so further kinds are additive. Display on each reproduces the exact message the old string carried, so log output is unchanged.

Both VARIANTS are #[non_exhaustive] as q9hv.19 asked. That blocks struct-literal construction outside the crate, which is the cost I flagged -- pkix-chain/tests/serde_round_trip.rs constructs both. Resolved with Error::profile_violation(kind) and Error::ocsp_delegation(kind), which tests, mocks and adapters need and which read better than a struct literal anyway.

The payoff is visible in the five tests that had to change, all of which were sniffing the string: reason.contains("critical"), contains("only id-kp-timeStamping"), contains("KeyUsage"), contains("issuer DN"), contains("signature"). All five are now assert_eq! against a named kind. The best illustration is the last: its comment read "the reason must point at the signature-binding failure, not the DN gate -- both surface as OcspDelegation but mean different things diagnostically". That is precisely the distinction the typed payload makes first-class rather than inferred from prose, and it is the DN-twin attack the binding exists to catch.

Serde: the old test turned on Cow content-based equality surviving Borrowed-to-Owned. It now round-trips every kind and additionally asserts no two kinds share a wire form -- otherwise caching an error and reloading it would silently lose the classification, which is the use case serde on these types is for.

Unaffected consumers: pkix-tlsrpt/src/classify.rs and both pkix-difftest oracles match with { .. }, so they needed no change -- which is the #[non_exhaustive] discipline working as intended.

Gates green: fmt, clippy, rustdoc, typos, 2357 tests, workspace feature powerset 241 combinations clean.
